BREAKING NEWS 🚨 

NPA Secures Final Forfeiture Of R100,000 Bribe In Tembisa Hospital Corruption Case

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) has secured a final forfeiture order for R100,000 allegedly offered as a bribe by former Tembisa Hospital official Zacharia Tshisele (pitctured).

Tshisele, who worked as an operational manager in the hospital’s theatre department, was arrested in November 2025 alongside Hawks Sergeant Papi Tsie. The pair allegedly handed R100,000 in cash to a Hawks investigating officer handling the Tembisa Hospital corruption investigation in an attempt to prevent Tshisele’s arrest and prosecution.

The money has now been forfeited to the state and will be paid into the Criminal Assets Recovery Account.

The alleged bribery attempt is linked to the broader investigation into corruption and procurement irregularities at Tembisa Hospital. The Special Investigating Unit (SIU) previously found that Tshisele allegedly received unlawful gratification from service providers between January 2020 and September 2023.

In November 2025, he repaid R13.5 million to the SIU, representing part of the money linked to the alleged corruption.

The SIU's wider investigation has uncovered approximately R122 million in alleged corrupt payments involving at least 15 current and former officials at the hospital and the Gauteng Department of Health.

Tshisele has also been linked to two alleged syndicates that secured hundreds of millions of rands in hospital contracts.
